Doc.Base64.Body: Switch between Encode and Decode with the radio buttons, or click “Choose file…” to encode a file's raw bytes directly instead of typed text. URL-safe alphabet and 76-character MIME line-wrapping are optional toggles. Decoding bytes that look like an image renders an inline preview automatically; decoding to text falls back to a hex dump if the bytes aren't valid UTF-8. Swap feeds the result back in as input and flips the direction, for a quick round-trip check.
Doc.Color.Body: Type or paste a colour as hex, rgb(), hsl() or hsv() — or pick one visually with either picker button — and every other notation updates live next to a swatch preview. The Contrast row reports the WCAG contrast ratio of that colour against both white and black, the number that tells you whether it's safe to use as text on either background.
Doc.Converter.Body: Choose a source and target format from the two dropdowns — JSON, XML or CSV — and swap them with the button in between. Paste into the left editor and the read-only right pane updates as you type or on Ctrl+Enter. Conversions route through a common internal model so JSON⇄XML round-trips losslessly; converting through CSV flattens nested structure into dotted keys, and an info banner appears whenever that lossy leg is involved.
Doc.Cron.Body: Type a standard five-field cron expression — minute, hour, day-of-month, month, day-of-week — and it's translated into a plain-English summary plus the next 10 times it will actually fire, shown in local time. That's the reliable way to tell apart expressions that look similar at a glance, like a job that fires every Sunday at midnight versus one that fires on the 1st of every month.
Doc.Diff.Body: Paste the original into the left editor and the changed version into the right one; a unified diff appears in the pane below shortly after you stop typing. Ignore-whitespace, ignore-case and ignore-blank-lines checkboxes each recompute immediately when toggled, for when formatting noise is getting in the way of the comparison you actually care about.
Doc.Formatter.Body: Works like the JSON and XML tools, but the format itself is auto-detected from what you paste — JSON, XML or CSV. Format, Minify and Validate all run against whichever format is detected, and the editor's syntax colouring switches to match once a document parses successfully. Use it when you don't know or don't care which format you're holding.
Doc.Hash.Body: Type text or choose a file, and every supported algorithm — MD5, SHA-1/256/384/512 and CRC32 — computes at once, each with its own copy button. Check “Use HMAC” and supply a key to switch every algorithm except CRC32 to an HMAC. Paste an expected value into “Compare to expected” to check it against every computed hash using a constant-time comparison; MD5 and SHA-1 are labelled checksum-only as a reminder they aren't fit for security use.
Doc.Json.Body: Paste JSON into the single editor, then use Format, Minify or Validate from the command bar. Invalid input is never cleared — the status bar points at the exact line and column instead. The indent stepper controls how many spaces Format uses, and syntax colouring updates as you type.
Doc.Jwt.Body: Paste a token to see its header and payload rendered as colourised JSON alongside the raw signature segment. exp/iat/nbf claims are humanised into a relative-time chip, and a warning banner flags an alg: none header or a mismatched typ. This tool explicitly never verifies the signature — a permanent banner says so, so a clean decode is never mistaken for a valid, trusted token.
Doc.Lorem.Body: Choose a unit — paragraphs, sentences or words — and a count, then Generate. Leave “Start with 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet…'” checked to keep the traditional opening line, or uncheck it to randomise every word. Output regenerates automatically whenever you change the unit, count or that checkbox.
Doc.Masker.Body: Paste text into the editor and detected personal information — emails, phone numbers, card numbers, keys and more — appears in the findings list beside it, each with a confidence level, a per-finding masking strategy dropdown and an include/exclude checkbox. A profile and confidence threshold decide what counts as a finding, and “Mask all”/“Mask none” toggle every finding at once. The editor only ever shows the masked result; the unmasked text stays in memory, is never written to disk, and copy always acts on the masked output.
Doc.NumberBase.Body: Decimal, hex, binary and octal boxes stay in sync — edit any one and the others update immediately. Choose a width (8/16/32/64-bit) and whether the value is signed, then click individual bits in the bit grid to toggle them directly. The bitwise playground applies AND, OR, XOR, NOT and single-bit shifts against a second operand you type in.
Doc.Password.Body: Set a length and which character classes to draw from — lowercase, uppercase, digits, symbols — optionally excluding look-alike characters like I, l, 1, O and 0, then Generate up to 500 passwords at once. The entropy line beneath the options reports the bits of randomness your current settings buy, so you can see whether making it longer or adding a character class actually helped. Nothing generated here is stored; closing the window forgets it.
Doc.Regex.Body: Type a .NET-flavour pattern and a subject; matches are highlighted inline in the read-only echo beneath the subject, and every captured group is listed in the groups table. Add a replacement pattern (e.g. $1) to preview what Regex.Replace would produce. IgnoreCase, Multiline, Singleline, IgnorePatternWhitespace and ECMAScript are all toggleable, and every match runs under a timeout so a catastrophic pattern can't hang the tool.
Doc.TextToolkit.Body: Pick an operation from the dropdown — case conversion (camelCase, snake_case, Title Case…), line operations (sort, dedupe, trim, number, reverse, join or split on a separator), or escape/unescape for JSON, C#, SQL, shell or regex — and the output pane updates as you type. “Use output as input” feeds the result back into the input box, so several operations can be chained one click at a time.
Doc.Timestamp.Body: A live “current time” row at the top ticks once a second. Paste an epoch value or almost any parseable date/time into Input — the epoch unit (seconds, milliseconds or microseconds) is auto-detected from the number's magnitude but can be overridden — and every representation (epoch seconds/millis, ISO 8601, RFC 1123, local time, UTC and a relative “3 hours ago” phrasing) updates together. “Use current time” fills Input with now.
Doc.Url.Body: One page, three sections picked from the Section dropdown. Percent-encoding shows RFC 3986 and form (space→+) encoding side by side, since the two disagree and that's a common source of bugs. HTML entities encodes text for safe embedding in markup. The URL parser splits a pasted URL into scheme, host, port, path and fragment, and lets you add, edit or remove query parameters in a live table that rebuilds the full URL as you go.
Doc.Uuid.Body: Choose a version — v4 (random), v7 (time-ordered), or the all-zero NIL — a display format (hyphenated, braced, parenthesised, compact, uppercase or Base64), and a count up to 1000, then Generate. Results land one per line in the read-only box, ready to copy individually or all at once.
Doc.Xml.Body: The same single-pane Format / Minify / Validate workflow as the JSON tool, fixed to XML. Malformed markup is left exactly as you pasted it — the status bar reports the line and column of the problem instead of clearing your text — and the indent width is adjustable from the command bar.

Settings.AccentTintDesc: काँच को टास्कबार के तटस्थ स्लेटी के बजाय आपके Windows एक्सेंट रंग से रंगें।
Settings.AlwaysOnTopDesc: फ़्लोटिंग रहते हुए डॉक को दूसरी विंडो के ऊपर रखता है। (किनारे पर लगे होने पर यह हमेशा ऊपर रहता है।)
Settings.AutoHide: किनारे पर लगे होने पर अपने आप छिपाएँ

Settings.BackupDesc: डॉक, उसके टूल और सारी सेटिंग्स एक फ़ाइल में सहेजें या वापस लाएँ — DevDX को दूसरे पीसी पर ले जाने का यही तरीका है।
Settings.CheckForUpdatesDesc: लॉन्च पर GitHub से पूछता है कि क्या कोई नया संस्करण उपलब्ध है। डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से बंद — जब तक यह चालू न हो, DevDX कोई नेटवर्क कनेक्शन नहीं बनाता।
Settings.DensityDesc: डॉक के आइकन और सेल कितने बड़े हैं। “मध्यम” Windows 11 टास्कबार से मेल खाता है।
Settings.GlassDesc: डॉक का ऐक्रेलिक कितना धुँधला है। कम रखने पर डेस्कटॉप ज़्यादा दिखता है।
Settings.HotkeyDesc: एक सिस्टम-व्यापी शॉर्टकट जो डॉक को सामने ले आता है — तब भी जब वह स्क्रीन के किनारे के पीछे छिपा हो।
Settings.ItemHotkeysDesc: अलग-अलग आइटम को अपना सिस्टम-व्यापी शॉर्टकट दें, जो आइकन के राइट-क्लिक मेन्यू से असाइन होता है। डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से बंद, क्योंकि हर शॉर्टकट बाकी सभी ऐप्स से वह संयोजन छीन लेता है।
Settings.LanguageDesc: DevDX की अपनी विंडो और मेन्यू की भाषा। यह तुरंत लागू होती है।
Settings.MagnifyDesc: कर्सर के गुज़रने पर आइकन बड़े होते हैं, macOS डॉक की तरह। यह वृद्धि पट्टी के भीतर ही रहती है, इसलिए डॉक का आकार कभी नहीं बदलता।
Settings.OpenIndicatorsDesc: जिस टूल की विंडो पहले से खुली है उसके नीचे एक बिंदु दिखाएँ। “खुली विंडो दोबारा इस्तेमाल करें” चालू हो तो क्लिक करने पर दूसरी विंडो खोलने के बजाय वही विंडो सामने आती है।
Settings.PositionDesc: इसे स्वतंत्र रूप से तैरने दें, या स्क्रीन के किसी किनारे से सटाकर लगाएँ।
Settings.ResetSectionDesc: सभी पिन किए गए टूल हटाएँ और डिफ़ॉल्ट डॉक वापस लाएँ।

Settings.SearchHotkeyDesc: एक सिस्टम-व्यापी शॉर्टकट जो आपके पिन किए आइटमों पर खोज बॉक्स खोलता है। जब तक आप एक असाइन न करें, बंद रहता है।
